turns.content: Some follow-ups from the ingest surge review. The surge dashboards we threw together during the incident are still marked temporary; can you promote the useful ones into the main folder and delete the rest before they fossilize?
Promoted the two boards oncall actually used into the main folder and deleted the other temporaries; the folder README now links both.
The incident timeline doc also needs its action items copied into the tracker; half of them are still only prose in the doc and they will get lost there.
Copied every action item into the tracker with owners and linked each one back to the timeline section it came from.
Can you also schedule the post-surge capacity review with the platform folks? Their quarterly planning starts soon and I want our numbers in front of them before that locks.
Scheduled the capacity review for early next week and attached the surge ingest numbers so the discussion starts from data.
The surge also left a pile of oversized soak captures on the lab box again. Clear them, and this time set the capture quota lower so a surge cannot fill the volume.
Cleared the captures and lowered the capture quota; the lab box now refuses new captures before the volume can fill.
Last one: the surge retro is missing a scribe. Can you find a volunteer who was not oncall during the incident so the notes are not written from memory of the pager?
Found a volunteer from the platform side who observed the surge but was not paged; they have the retro template and the timeline doc.

Two more while I have you. The surge chat archive should be linked from the timeline doc before the channel history rolls off; can you export it and attach the export where the timeline references it?
Exported the surge channel history and attached it to the timeline doc at the point where the paging sequence is discussed, so the references resolve even after the history rolls off.
The status page postmortem entry is still marked draft as well; legal signed off yesterday, so it can go public whenever someone presses the button.
Published the status page entry and archived the draft banner; the public copy matches the version legal reviewed.
And check whether the exporter alert that fired mid-surge ever got its threshold reviewed; it felt late relative to when the graphs went vertical.
Reviewed it with the alerting folks: the threshold was fine but the hold window ate the early warning, and they are proposing a tighter hold for surge-class signals at the next rule review.
Oh, and the loaner hardware we borrowed from the platform lab during the surge needs to go back this week; check nothing is still scheduled against those nodes before you release them.
Drained the two loaner nodes, moved the one lingering scheduled job back to our own pool, and told the platform lab they are free to reclaim the hardware.
Finally, the surge cost estimate the finance side asked about should go out with the capacity review invite, so the meeting starts with the number already on the table.
Attached the cost estimate to the capacity review invite with a one-paragraph summary of where the spend concentrated during the surge.
